N-heterocycles with N-fluorenyl substituents are more likely to dimerize to tricyclocarbene than to Wanzlick dication, whereas the corresponding pentafluorobenzylated derivatives are more likely to undergo the Wanzlick equilibrium.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nature of the precursor to the NHC, i.e., the azolinium salt versus the NHC adduct, determines whether or not the N-fluorinated heterocycle can be formed.
the fate of N-heterocycles is determined by their electronic structure and the presence of an activating substituent.
NHC dimerization is suppressed when N-substituents are bulky and/or when the N-substituent is capable of stabilizing the NHC in its azomethine imine form.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Wanzlick equilibrium is a dynamic process and that the outcome can be manipulated by subtle structural changes.
the NHCs can be divided into two groups depending on the nature of the substituents at the N-atom, with one group being prone to the Wanzlick equilibrium and the other not.
the NHCs derived from azolinium salts or NHC adducts are not the same and that the NHC generated from an adduct is not the same as the NHC generated in situ from an azolinium precursor.
